attention_route.cls_query: native last-block CLS query, never replaced by text
attention_route.cls_slot: fixed gate 1, never trainable, excluded from LS
attention_route.conditional_path_use: training only; not used at inference
attention_route.gate_sharing: one 196-d patch gate shared by the 12 vision heads
attention_route.keys_values: native last-block keys/values, shared by both paths
attention_route.renormalisation: a_cond = (a * m_full) / sum_p (a * m_full); no detached denominator, no clamp

config.candidate_rule: fixed image: every candidate text uses its own patch gate; fixed text: every candidate image is scored with the gate of that (text, image) pair; positives and negatives follow the identical rule
config.caption_stream: reference prefix draw caption.split(". ")[:k], k ~ randint(1, n)

chunking.note: the conditional CLS runs tile by tile in fp32; no [B,B,12,197] or [B,B,768] activation is ever resident

config.ddp_route: per-rank anchor means + autograd-aware gather + standard DDP averaging; no world-size factor

gate.cls_self_gate: fixed 1, not trainable, not in the sparse term
gate.gate_bias: single trainable scalar initialised to log(8)
gate.gate_forward: hard straight-through: hard = (p >= 0.5), m = hard + (p - p.detach())

config.grader: none: LG never touches the gate, LA touches the shared CLIP parameters and the gate, LS (mean of the positive pairs patch gates) touches only the gate
config.loss_combination: 5*(LG_i2t+LG_t2i) + 5*(LA_i2t+LA_t2i) + LS, LS = mean of the 196 patch gates on the true positive pairs
config.precision: fp32 master weights; bf16 autocast for the first 11 visual blocks and the text transformer; the final visual CLS core (ln_1, Q/K/V, the native softmax, the caption gate, the renormalisation, out_proj, both residuals, ln_2/MLP, ln_post, visual.proj), the text projection, the normalisation, the scores and every loss are explicitly fp32
config.statistics_scope: rank0 local batch unless the field name says otherwise
config.text_source: ln_final sequence, EOT = argmax(token ids), native text_projection in fp32

two_paths.attention: Norm(ln_post(CLS after the same last block with the native CLS attention weights renormalised by the caption gate) @ visual.proj)
two_paths.native: Norm(ln_post(CLS after the native last block) @ visual.proj)

config.view: image_a only (reference openai-clip _transform(224)); no second view, no new augmentation task
config.x11_source: tokens ENTERING the last visual block, from ONE visual forward over blocks 0..10

gate_config.cls_self_gate: fixed 1, not trainable, not in the sparse term
gate_config.gate_bias: single trainable scalar initialised to log(8)
gate_config.gate_forward: hard straight-through: hard = (p >= 0.5), m = hard + (p - p.detach())

cost.chunking_note: 32x64 tiles were chosen from a measured comparison before the run: 8x32 gave 6.3 s/step and 32x64 gave 2.0 s/step at the same 40.7 GiB peak, with losses agreeing to 1e-3 floating-point summation-order noise

gate_behaviour.cls_slot_gate: fixed 1, never trainable, excluded from the sparse term
findings: the gate closes progressively and monotonically: 100.6 of 196 patch gates are kept at step 25 and 64.2 at step 500
the gate NEVER collapses: all-off and all-on fractions are exactly 0.0 at every heavy-log step, so it is not a constant mask
about 11.8 percent of the straight-through probabilities sit within 0.05 of the 0.5 threshold at step 500, so individual gate coordinates can flip under noise

the gate varies about 2.4 times more across images (same text) than across texts (same image) at step 500 (0.2222 vs 0.0945): in this run the learned gate is predominantly an image-side selector even though the text is the only conditional input

provenance_corrections.reason: the first student file carried only {"model": ...} without completed_steps, which the Urban-1k evaluator refuses to accept; the export tool was fixed to record the step count, the student was re-exported with identical weights, and BOTH evaluations were re-run so that every reported number refers to the final file

verdict.query_count_note: 0.10 pp of the 5000 COCO image queries is 5 queries (each 1/5000); 0.02 pp of the 25000 COCO text queries is 5 queries (each 1/25000). The two protocols have different denominators and the same pp figure therefore means a different number of queries.
verdict.rule: COCO I2T R@1 >= 0.6058 and T2I R@1 >= 0.41236, at least one strictly higher; compared on the UNROUNDED values
verdict.urban_query_count_note: Urban-1k compares 1000 images against 1000 captions, so 1.0 pp there is 10 image queries and 10 text queries
